title: Cyber Resilience Act product security
description: Questions for the product security owner and repository checks for products with digital elements under Regulation (EU) 2024/2847. Reporting under Art. 14 has applied since 11 September 2026; the other obligations apply from 11 December 2027 (Art. 71(2)). These rules do not establish conformity.

sources.title: European Commission, The Cyber Resilience Act: summary of the legislative text

rules.instruction: Ask the legal owner whether the product is a product with digital elements made available on the EU market, and whether the organization acts as manufacturer, importer, distributor or open-source software steward (Art. 3).
rules.verification: Link the recorded answer from the change.
rules.manual: The product's status and the organization's role are a legal assessment.

rules.instruction: Generate for each release a software bill of materials in a commonly used machine-readable format that covers at least the top-level dependencies (Annex I, Part II, point 1; applicable from 11 December 2027).
rules.verification: task verify checks that a CI workflow generates an SBOM; open a release and check that its SBOM lists the shipped top-level dependencies.

rules.instruction: Keep a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy and a contact address for reporting vulnerabilities (Annex I, Part II, points 5 and 6; applicable from 11 December 2027).
rules.verification: Open the published policy and check that it gives the contact address and the handling steps.

rules.instruction: Make the default configuration of the changed component secure, with a way to reset the product to its original state (Annex I, Part I, point 2(b); applicable from 11 December 2027).
rules.verification: Install the release with default settings in a test and review the exposed services, credentials and permissions.
rules.manual: Default exposure shows when the release is installed with default settings.

rules.instruction: Distribute security updates through a secure update mechanism, automatic where applicable (Annex I, Part II, point 7; applicable from 11 December 2027).
rules.verification: Check in a test that the client verifies the authenticity of an update artifact before installing it.
rules.manual: Update authenticity is checked by installing an update artifact in a test.

rules.instruction: Ask the product owner for the support period during which vulnerabilities will be handled, at least five years unless the product is expected to be in use for less (Art. 13(8); applicable from 11 December 2027), and record it in the product documentation.
rules.verification: Check that the product documentation states the support period.
rules.manual: The support period is the product owner's decision, written in product documentation that may live outside the repository.
